sections.html:
The Wexford County Register of Deeds is at 437 E. Division St., Cadillac, on the second floor of the older section of the courthouse. The main entrance and parking lot are behind the building. Mail goes to P.O. Box 303, Cadillac, MI 49601, and the phone is (231) 779-9455.

To drive in from downtown Cadillac, head east on Harris Street, go four blocks, and look to the left.

You can mail a filing. Send it with the fees and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for the return. State law does not allow recording a photocopy, so the sheet you send must be the original with original signatures.

Every document costs $30.00 to record, however many pages it has. That amount includes the Michigan remonumentation fee and the Register's automation fee, and it has been the statewide figure since October 1, 2016. The office takes cash, checks and credit cards. Make checks payable to Register of Deeds.

  • Tax certification, $5.00, is required on every warranty deed and land contract.
  • A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per instrument beyond the base $30.00.
  • A fixture filing costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $1.00 a page, and certifying a document is $5.00.
  • Name searches cost $5.00 each plus $0.50 per year. UCC searches are $6.00 a name, and state, federal, MESC or judgment searches are $3.00 a name.
  • A track index request is $50 an hour, or $25 for half an hour.
  • Emailing a request adds a $3.00 convenience fee.

The counter also sells fill-in-the-blank quit claim, warranty and mineral deeds and non-construction liens for $5.00 each. Staff do not draft legal papers or advise on wording, and the office suggests hiring an attorney for any deed.

The county prints a table that splits each $500 price band into a state share and a county share. One check payable to the Wexford County Register of Deeds can cover transfer tax, tax certification and recording together.

Each further $500 band repeats the same pair of amounts. The printed table stops at $100,000, so for a typical home price, ask the counter staff for the exact tax before you write the check. If the sale is exempt, the exemption must be cited on the deed itself: MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax.

sections.h2: What a deed must contain to be recorded
sections.html:
The county posts seventeen numbered rules with statute citations, and every deed is checked against them. The ones that trip people up most:

  • Names typed or printed under the original signatures must match the names in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Each deed or assignment gives the grantee's street or post office address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Page one leaves 2.5 inches blank at the top, and every page keeps a half inch around the other edges. Ink is black, type is at least 10 point, and the paper is white, at least 20 pound, and between letter and legal size.
  • The first line of print says what the paper does, such as a warranty deed.
  • If the deed claims survivorship, a certified death certificate or proof of death is already recorded or referenced by liber and page.
  • A court order carries the clerk's certification and seal.

Unplatted land needs two more statements. One says whether the right to make further divisions under the Land Division Act is being conveyed. The other is the Michigan right to farm notice about nearby agricultural operations.

Most paper types can be e-recorded. Court certified documents and anything needing tax certification are excluded, so warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, their assignments, plats and condominium documents must still be filed on paper.

E-recording is processed from 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M., Monday to Friday, except county holidays. Payment goes by ACH under vendor agreements. Only fees set by state and local statute reach the county, and vendors can add their own charges. A submission that breaks the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected, and a filer who violates the state's e-recording standards is cut off until further notice. The vendors in use are CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm.

sections.h2: Records affected by the 2024 cyber incident
sections.html:
A cyber incident on November 5, 2024 kept the office from recovering under 5% of documents first recorded between August 14, 2024 and October 30, 2024. If you sent papers for recording in that stretch, call the office to learn whether yours survived or must be recorded again. A seller who closed in those months should make that call before listing.

The online land records search is hosted through the county website, and the office's holdings go back to 1864. Duplicate microfilm sits in underground storage in Grand Rapids. Once a document is recorded, anyone may request a copy for $1.00 a page. The office will fax prepaid copies but will not email them.

The office also runs a Fraud Notify service that watches for recordings under a name or business name. Ask the office how to enroll.

MCL 211.135 keeps a warranty deed from being recorded until a treasurer's certificate shows the prior five years of tax paid. That is what the $5.00 certification line buys. Any balance owed on the parcel has to be settled by closing, so check with the treasurer early if you think something is outstanding.

Family situations come up often. If a spouse dies and both names were on the deed, bring a certified death certificate and the fee. No new deed is issued, because the office only records. A paid-off mortgage produces a discharge from the lender, not a deed. Adding or removing a name affects divorce, borrowing, taxes and probate, so talk to an attorney first. Once the sale closes, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor a transfer notice (MCL 211.27a).

A cash sale does not change any of this. The deed still needs the same signatures, the same tax certification and the same fees, but it skips lender paperwork and the delays that come with underwriting.

Wexford County sits in the Northern Lower Peninsula and holds much of the Manistee National Forest. Population is 34,445, with 16,924 housing units. About 80.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle value of an owned home is $170,400, and median household income is $61,085. Many parcels are rural, so the land division and farm notice statements above come up more often here than they would on a platted city lot.

faqs.q: What is the per-document recording charge in Wexford County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00, which includes the Michigan remonumentation and Register of Deeds automation fees. Warranty deeds add $5.00 for tax certification, and discharges covering several instruments add $3.00 for each.

faqs.q: Can a warranty deed go through e-recording in Wexford County?
faqs.a: No. Warranty deeds and land contracts need tax certification, so they go in on paper: the original, with original signatures, delivered or mailed with fees and a stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: Will Wexford County staff advise me on wording my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office prepares no legal documents and gives no legal advice. It sells blank fill-in forms for $5.00 and recommends an attorney.

faqs.q: How can I find the owner of a Wexford County parcel?
faqs.a: Ask the County Equalization Department or the assessor for the city, township or village. They can give the name on the tax roll, which may differ from the owner, and that name opens a search of the Register's records.

faqs.q: Do I get a new deed after paying off a Wexford County mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage to be recorded. Your deed remains the one from purchase, and a recorded copy costs $1.00 per page.
